title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent-to-Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) that compares LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Under a frozen plan we ran 200 stratified paired trials in a Dockerized Mininet emulator with a deterministic validator and gpt-5-mini. Observed confirmatory outcomes: baseline verifier-accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier-accepted = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729), exact paired-test p = 1.0. This null result follows directly from an explicit, preregistered generation_semantics choice: one shared LLM candidate per task was generated and evaluated under both arms ("shared_initial_candidate"), so no repair calls were invoked (repair_attempts = 0). We archive all preregistration and execution artifacts (task manifests, LLM outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts) with SHA-256 hashes so others can reproduce and run follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint, expand validator coverage, or vary model sampling.

sections.introduction: Generative models can translate operator intent into device configuration, promising automation for network operations (NetOps). However, unguarded outputs risk reachability loss, policy violations, or availability regressions. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines reduce operational risk by combining LLM generation with deterministic validation and bounded repairs. Prior benchmarks probe pieces of this architecture but seldom provide fully preregistered, artifact-backed, paired comparisons with deterministic reconciliation. We preregistered and ran GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1 to quantify whether a guarded GVR pipeline reduces operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation under a clearly specified emulator and validator. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run (200 pairs) with frozen analysis and public artifacts; (2) deterministic reconciliation and full per-episode hashing; (3) an artifact-grounded account of the observed null paired difference and explicit boundary conditions that produced it.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps and verifier-assisted pipelines have been explored in recent literature (NetConfEval; OpsEval; NetEval) and in AIOps surveys. Work in software engineering and automated repair motivates generate–validate–repair patterns, but prior experiments often lack preregistration, deterministic artifact publication, or paired within-task designs that avoid sampling confounds. Our study adopts the GVR architecture but emphasizes preregistration, deterministic auditing, and explicit boundary-condition interpretation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) froze research question, sampling, validator rules, contamination thresholds (≥80% token-overlap exclusion), retry policy, analysis plan, and stopping rules. Key preregistered and executed design choice: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM-produced candidate per task used for both arms), recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Execution harness and resources. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt-5-mini. Emulation and validator. A Dockerized Mininet emulator and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parsed configurations, enforced workflow-safety constraints (e.g., "must be down for MTU/VLAN change"), executed reachability/policy probes, and returned verifier-accept/reject. Task bank and sampling. Confirmatory bank = 200 tasks stratified across five protocol-focus clusters × two interaction modalities (≈20 tasks per cluster). We pre-specified that infrastructure failures (container crashes) would be logged and excluded from the primary analysis; none occurred. Artifact archival and reproducibility. All raw artifacts (task manifests, LLM outputs, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, execution_manifest, analysis artifacts) are published with SHA-256 hashes. Representative pointers: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA-256 f8de4d6e1a625e42...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA-256 9235bce7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 a40e96e2...). The initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Analysis plan (preregistered). Primary estimand: paired difference in the binary operational-failure indicator (1 if reachability loss or policy violation observed; 0 otherwise). Inference: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for CI and an exact paired contingency test where appropriate. Contamination and prechecks. Automated contamination detection (token-overlap) was applied per preregistration; no confirmatory tasks were excluded.
sections.results: Execution. The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per confirmatory task), failed_episode_count = 0 (execution_manifest). Scoring. Confirmatory scoring: baseline verifier-accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier-accepted = 200/200. Paired contingency (archived): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 7bc1bd2a...). Primary inference. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Exact paired-contingency assessment (McNemar two-sided) p = 1.0. Repair activity. No repairs were applied on any confirmatory episode: repair_applied = false for all 200 confirmatory tasks (see execution/scoring/*.json files; representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, SHA-256 9235bce7...). Deterministic reconciliation. All bookkeeping and call-accounting checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.discussion: Why a null paired difference? The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM candidate per task used for both arms) intentionally reduced model calls but mechanically prevents observing repair-driven improvements because the same candidate was evaluated under both arms; since repair attempts were not triggered (repair_attempts = 0), baseline and guarded acceptance counts were identical. This design choice was preregistered and executed; the observed null therefore documents a concrete boundary condition rather than a general negative statement about GVR. Statistical test choice. The preregistration specified a paired plan and bootstrap CI; for the realized 2×2 contingency we reported the exact paired-contingency result (McNemar) because it is the appropriate paired-test for binary outcomes in a contingency table; we archive the contingency counts and the bootstrap parameters (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) so readers can reproduce both analyses. Practical implications and follow-ups. To detect repair value experimentally, follow-ups should (a) use independent-condition-generation (separate LLM candidates per arm), (b) sample multiple stochastic generations (temperature or sampling seeds) or multiple models, (c) broaden validator/emulator coverage (increase realistic failure exposure), or (d) evaluate in production-like heterogeneous firmware/device stacks. Our published artifacts permit deterministic reproduction and these targeted follow-ups. Reproducibility. All artifacts (task manifests, responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, execution_manifest, analysis artifacts) are provided with SHA-256 hashes to enable deterministic reanalysis; representative file paths and SHA-256 values are listed in the evidence bundle and above.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation (200 confirmatory pairs) comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline with gpt-5-mini. Under the explicit, preregistered shared-generation semantics and tested emulator+validator scope, both arms produced verifier-acceptable configurations on all confirmatory tasks (200/200 each), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and McNemar p = 1.0. Because the design produced identical LLM candidates for both arms (repair_attempts = 0), the confirmatory test is boundary-conditional; it does not imply GVR lacks value generally. All preregistration and execution artifacts (with SHA-256 hashes) are archived to permit reproducible reanalysis and planned follow-ups that relax the shared-generation constraint or broaden model and validator diversity.

All raw artifacts, provenance traces, and analysis scripts are archived and hashed to permit deterministic reproduction and follow-up experiments.
limitations: Emulation and synthetic-task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor-like templates in a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production firmware/device diversity is not represented.
Single-model scope: only gpt-5-mini was evaluated in the confirmatory run; results do not generalize across model families or sampling regimes.

Shared-generation preregistration choice: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate per task evaluated by both arms) was preregistered and executed; because no repairs were invoked (repair_attempts = 0) baseline and guarded outputs were identical, mechanically preventing observation of repair-driven differences in this run.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set and probes; gaps in validator rules or emulator realism limit construct validity relative to production environments.

Power-plan assumption violated: the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure; observed baseline success = 100% in confirmatory bank and thus the preregistered MDE target could not be assessed.
Contamination-detection limits: automated token-overlap checks flagged 0 confirmatory tasks, but undiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be fully excluded.
